title: 'Lest we forget' flag to fly at Queen's Park after advocacy work by New Dundee, Ont., veteran
summary: Donald Eenkooren says he's happy but a bit surprised to learn the "Lest we forget" flag will fly at Queen's Park in Toronto this Remembrance Day, although it won't be on one of the three official…

image.caption: The 'Lest we forget' flag is white with a bright red poppy in the middle as seen at this Kitchener, Ont., Remembrance Day ceremony in 2024. (Kate Bueckert/CBC)

blocks.text: Kitchener-Waterloo

Donald Eenkooren says he's happy but a bit surprised to learn the "Lest we forget" flag will fly at Queen's Park in Toronto this Remembrance Day, although it won't be on one of the three official ceremonial flagpoles at the Ontario Legislature.
Donald Eenkooren has been advocating to have flag flown widely for Remembrance Day
Eenkooren, a veteran from New Dundee, has been advocating to have the flag flown across Canada on Nov. 11, reaching out to all provincial and territorial premiers over the past year.
All the provinces except Ontario and Quebec agreed to his request.
He said he began advocating to have it flown in more places three years ago, starting with the Ontario government.
"I tried for three years to try to get Ontario to change their mind," Eenkooren told CBC News.

"I just wanted to advocate that we do have a flag and that it should be proudly flown as much as we can, and the remembrance of the veterans of the past, present, and the ones who paid the ultimate sacrifice to this great country."

Donald Eenkooren, a retired chief petty officer, 2nd class, and a Canadian Armed Forces veteran, speaks at the raising of the 'Lest we forget' flag at Parliament Hill in Ottawa in 2025. (Submitted by the office of MP Tim Louis)
The simple white flag — with a large red poppy in the middle and the words "Lest we forget" in bold, black lettering — was created by The Royal Canadian Legion.

It was flown for the first time during Veterans' Week last year at Parliament Hill in Ottawa. Eenkooren and members of the New Hamburg Legion were in that city last week to raise it for the second year in a row, along with Kitchener-Conestoga MP Tim Louis.

Flag to fly 'on Ontario Legislature grounds,' MPP says
Eenkooren said he received a phone call last week from Waterloo MPP Catherine Fife telling him the flag would be flown at Queen's Park this year after all.

Fife brought forward a petition in the Legislature to raise the flag, especially in light of the four service members who died at CFB Wainwright, a Canadian Forces Base in east-central Alberta, on Oct. 17.
"I'm very pleased that Ontario will recognize this important symbol of remembrance and I know that veterans will appreciate this sign of respect," Fife said in a release.
She called the decision to fly the flag "a meaningful win for our veterans, their families and everyone committed to honouring those who served and sacrificed for our country."
Only three flags will continue to be on ceremonial flagpoles in front of Queen's Park on a permanent basis: Canada, Ontario and Franco-Ontarian.
Julie Rosenberg, a spokesperson for Speaker Donna Skelly, said in an email that those three flags are outlined in the Ontario Legislative Assembly Flag Policy.
"Every year, in recognition of Remembrance Day, the flags at Queen's Park are flown at half-mast in accordance with Ontario's flag protocol," Rosenberg said.
Other flags, including the "Lest we forget" one, will go elsewhere on the property.
Fife said she had "secured a commitment from the premier's office" for the flag to be "flown on Ontario Legislature grounds."
Premier Doug Ford's office said the flag will be on stage as people speak during the Remembrance Day ceremony.
Looking to honour veterans
Eenkooren served 33 years in the Canadian Armed Forces, first as a marine engineer and later in military intelligence, completing several tours overseas and at home.

Eenkooren, right, raised the 'Lest we forget' flag on Parliament Hill for the first time on Oct. 31, 2025, at the start of Veterans' Week. It happened after years of advocacy from Eenkooren, who wants the flag raised in more public spaces across the country. (Royal Canadian Legion Branch 532 New Hamburg)
His decades of service inspired him to find new ways to honour veterans.
"My career was mostly into peacekeeping, but the Canadian Forces are also involved in domestic situations like forest fires and floods," he said.
"People don't really see us out there until something drastically happens, like CFB Wainwright."
Eenkooren said his focus is now on getting municipal governments to also fly the flag.

"I talked to a lot of people and they said this should have happened a long time ago," he said. "It's hard work but a worthy cause for the veterans, and trying to get all of Canada to remember and to never forget the veterans."
With files from Lauren Kuivenhoven
